headline: VIDEOCON INDUSTRIES: Supreme Court dismisses Twinstar's appeals; Rs 2,962.02 cr plan stays set aside, matter back to CoC
facts: Supreme Court order dated November 16, 2026 dismissed Civil Appeal Nos. 894, 512 and 509 of 2022 filed by Twinstar Technologies Limited, the Successful Resolution Applicant (SRA).
The NCLAT judgment of 05.01.2022 stands. It set aside approval of the SRA plan (total outlay Rs. 2,962.02 crores) and remitted the matter to the Committee of Creditors (CoC).

The Court held the plan breached Section 30(2)(b) of the IBC and Regulation 38(1)(b). Dissenting financial creditors were to be paid through NCDs of Rs. 2,700 crores face value, coupon 6.65 per cent, redeemable up to the sixth year, not in cash.
Admitted claims were Rs. 64,838.63 crores, a haircut of 95.85 per cent. Liquidation value was Rs. 2,568.13 crores. Operational creditors were to get 0.72 per cent.

Appeals by promoter Venugopal Dhoot and the VIL Vendors Association over the foreign oil and gas assets were dismissed. The Court held subsidiary assets are not VIL's assets under the Explanation to Section 18. The Vendors Association got liberty to pursue other remedies.

The Court said the CoC may reconsider the plan and need not confine itself to the SRA's existing plan. It may invite fresh plans. The CoC had resolved on 12.01.2022 to invite fresh expressions of interest.

The foreign oil and gas assets (Brazil, Indonesia) are held outside VIL. The filing mentions 8 per cent equity in VIL going to financial creditors under the old plan; it says nothing on the fate of existing equity under any new plan.
